deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio continues Riemann's 'Blatt 10' (previous page) and then opens 'Blatt 11', the essay 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', dated 'Gefunden am 1. März 1853'. That essay was printed in the Nachlass section of the Werke (Dedekind and Weber, 1876).

(a) End of Blatt 10. On the previous page Riemann listed four 'causes' behind the Newtonian explanation of gravitation. Cause 3 is a field g(x,t) of accelerating force at every point of space.
- He now seeks this field in the state of motion of a homogeneous substance that fills all of infinite space continuously.
- His hypothesis (stated in words): the substance's velocity u(x,t) has the same direction as the force it is to explain, and its speed is proportional to the force's magnitude. In modern terms, u(x,t) = k g(x,t) for a constant k.
- Equivalently, the substance is a 'physical space' whose points move within geometric space.
- Programme: first find the conditions the motion of the smallest parts of the substance must satisfy to reproduce the phenomena; then find the causes from which those motions can be explained.

(b) A bracketed fragment breaks off at a gap ('Lücke'). It reads: divide the region containing ponderable points into elements dT, and denote the gravitational strength of element dT by dm, and the distance ...
- Completion (mine, conjectural, not on the page): presumably he goes on to the Newtonian potential V(x) = ∫ dm/r with r = |x - x'|, so that g = grad V, with a sign convention. This would give u = k grad V.
- This matches the previous page, which identifies dη/dt with the velocity components of the substance's motion and V with the potential at time t.

(c) Blatt 11 is the introduction to the 'New mathematical principles' essay and is purely programmatic.
- Aim: to penetrate beyond the foundations laid by Galileo and Newton into the interior of nature.
- A correction reformulates this: to reduce those foundations to a deeper ground, giving mathematical physics a common foundation.
- He grants the speculation has no immediate practical use for astronomy.
- The ground of Newton's general laws of motion lies in the inner state of ponderable bodies, to be inferred by analogy from our own inner perception: new 'Vorstellungsmassen' (masses of ideas) continually arise in us.
- The next page continues with the Herbartian argument and the hypothesis of a substance continually flowing into ponderable atoms.

No actual computation is carried out on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors; there is no derivation on the page.
The definition at the end of Blatt 10 is left incomplete at a gap ('Lücke'), so the intended formula (presumably the Newtonian potential ∫ dm/r) is not actually written.

results.what: Hypothesis that the gravitational acceleration field equals, up to a constant factor, the velocity field of a space-filling homogeneous medium (ether), u = k g.
results.modern_name: Aether/sink-flow (hydrodynamic) model of gravitation; kinetic-ether gravitation
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Nachlass, published 1876). Related hydrodynamic or sink theories are credited to Euler (speculative), C. A. Bjerknes and Yarkovsky (1870s-1880s).

results.what: Programmatic introduction to 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (dated 1 March 1853), seeking a common foundation for mathematical physics beyond Galileo and Newton via Herbartian psychology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript of the well-known Naturphilosophie fragments printed in Riemann's collected works. The page contains only verbal hypotheses and an incomplete definition, with no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The point-mass potential 1/r is harmonic away from the origin (equals 0). This is the basis of the potential V = ∫ dm/r presumably intended in the truncated definition.
The gradient of 1/r has magnitude 1/r^2 (result 0), i.e. the inverse-square accelerating force of cause 4.

The flux of the inverse-square field through a sphere equals 4*pi, independent of radius. This is consistent with the next page's (1/4pi)∫ dP/dp dS mass formula and with an incompressible sink flow u = k g.

transcription_corrections: Page header 'Nat. Ph. 17.' at top right and the circled folio number '9' are omitted from the transcription.
The pencil margin note reads roughly '[... fehlt der Anfang von Blatt 9]'. Its first words are only partly legible; the ending 'Anfang von Blatt 9' is fairly clear.
'Gefunden am 1. März 1853' stands in the right column beside the title, not below the author line.
The margin note '[meinen Abhandlungen]' is placed next to the line 'Ich werde daher . . .'; the reading is uncertain.
